exposure: use of an innovative vaginal educator
outcome: bioelectrical activity of pelvic floor muscles (measured by root mean square, peak root mean square, area values, % maximal voluntary contraction, median frequency)
urinary incontinence status (measured by ICIQ-Short Form)
cohort: 30 women were assessed, with analysis considering factors such as age, childbirth history, sexual activity, urinary incontinence, and menopausal status.
finding: The innovative vaginal educator increased the electromyographic activity of the pelvic floor muscles, particularly in the neutral pelvic position, with benefits for older, multiparous, and sexually active women.
